text: Git branching is an important skill for developers who use version control. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. When you start a new task, you create a feature branch. This keeps your work separate and safe. After you finish, you can merge your changes back into the main branch. Many teams use pull requests to review the code before merging. This workflow helps everyone stay organised and avoid mistakes. If something goes wrong, you can easily go back to an earlier version. Learning how to use branches well makes teamwork smoother and keeps your project clean.
